epistemic_gaps: The sample size is very small (n=21), limiting generalizability.
The study focused on lower-body training; results may not apply to other muscle groups.

The primary outcomes measured were mechanistic/surrogate endpoints (muscle fiber cross-sectional area, satellite cells, anabolic signaling) rather than direct long-term functional performance outcomes (though both groups gained strength, the difference was in hypertrophy and cellular markers).
primary_claim: Regular cold-water immersion (10C for 10 minutes) after lower-body resistance training significantly attenuated gains in muscle fiber cross-sectional area and satellite cell number, and blunted anabolic signaling (mTOR and p70S6K activation) for up to two days post-training, compared to active recovery, in physically active men over 12 weeks.
